jobs.title: Global Principal Electrical Design Engineer - Data Center Segment
jobs.description: Eaton has been a key player in the Middle East for 40 years. In July 2024, we announced the construction of a new sustainable campus in Dubai, which will bring together our commercial, manufacturing, and support functions, providing room for future growth. About Eaton Eaton is a power management company where we provide energy-efficient solutions that help our customers effectively manage electrical, hydraulic and mechanical power more efficiently, safely and sustainably. Eaton is dedicated to improving the quality of life and the environment through the use of power management technology and services. Eaton has approximately 96,000 employees and sells products to customers in more than 175 countries. Eaton's Global Data Center Segment is focused on helping data centers realize real business benefits today while optimizing their operations for the future. With the rise of big data, edge computing and cloud, data centers are under pressure to be more high-performing, sustainable and cost-effective than ever, without compromising resilience or security. At the same time, new opportunities and revenue streams require faster speed-to-market. With our digital intelligence, world-class cyber-secure products and services, reliable, compatible solutions and engineering expertise, we help data centers realize real business benefits today while optimizing their operations for the future. Within this segment, Eaton has an opening for a Global Principal Electrical Design Engineer – Data Center Segment. The role serves as Eaton’s senior technical authority for electrical system design across global data center and mission‑critical projects. The role provides strategic and hands‑on engineering leadership from early concept development through detailed design, construction, and project closeout, ensuring technical excellence, safety, compliance, and scalability across global regions. This role influences Eaton’s global electrical design direction, standards, and best practices while supporting complex hyperscale and enterprise data center programs and collaborating with multidisciplinary teams, clients, and regional engineering organizations. What You’ll Do Global Electrical Design Authority Act as global subject matter expert and technical authority for electrical systems within Eaton’s Data Centre portfolio. Lead and support the design of complex electrical infrastructure for hyperscale and enterprise data centers from concept through execution. Provide expert guidance on MV and LV distribution, transformers, UPS architecture, protection and coordination, grounding, and system resilience strategies. Standards, Governance & Design Quality Develop, implement, and govern global electrical design standards, reference architectures, and quality frameworks. Ensure all designs align with North American standards (NEC, NFPA, IEEE, UL) and applicable IEC and international standards. Perform peer reviews and validation of electrical engineering deliverables across regions to ensure consistency, compliance, and technical rigor. Serve as final escalation point for complex or high‑risk electrical design challenges. Global Project & Stakeholder Engagement Collaborate within a multidisciplinary global engineering environment on projects of varying complexity and scale. Support bids, proposals, and execution phases by providing advanced electrical engineering expertise. Represent Eaton as a senior technical authority in internal and client-facing meetings, workshops, and design reviews. Participate in global site visits to assess electrical installations, construction quality, and commissioning readiness. Innovation, Value Engineering & Continuous Improvement Lead value engineering initiatives to optimize cost, performance, reliability, and constructability while maintaining system resilience. Evaluate and integrate emerging technologies and architectures in response to increasing power densities, AI/HPC loads, and resilience requirements. Contribute to continuous improvement of global electrical design approaches and delivery models. Knowledge Sharing & Technical Leadership Mentor and support the development of electrical engineering capability across global teams. Promote best practices, technical rigor, and consistent electrical design methodologies across regions and business units. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering from an accredited institution. 10+ years of electrical engineering experience with significant exposure to mission‑critical facilities and data center environments. Skills Deep expertise in MV/LV distribution systems, UPS architectures, transformers, grounding, protection schemes, and system coordination. Strong working knowledge of North American electrical codes (NEC, NFPA, IEEE, UL) and IEC standards. Demonstrated ability to operate as a senior technical authority within global, matrixed organizations. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to influence senior stakeholders and clients. Proven capability in program management, change management execution, and governance across global or matrixed organizations. Proven experience operating at a global or enterprise level, supporting multi‑region delivery models. Lead clarification and resolution of complex technical, commercial, and execution issues. Escalate effectively when required, ensuring speed, transparency, and leadership alignment. Ability to travel internationally as required. Strong technical, commercial, and analytical capability. Proven leadership, stakeholder engagement, and cross‑regional collaboration skills. Self‑directed with strong decision‑making and problem‑solving ability Fluent in English with the ability to engage effectively with diverse global teams. What We Offer You Being part of a company that has been in business for more than 100 years, is well known in the industry, and has a major impact on the energy industry Work in a company that is commitment to Inclusion & Diversity and Sustainability Annual mentoring program, Eaton University, a reward, and recognition system Ongoing Learning and Career Development Opportunities in a global company. Build your career and apply internally for our open positions worldwide Strong, agile and diverse team locally and globally Strong processes and state-of-the-art systems and tools Structured employee development processes, open feedback culture with development plans Detailed induction support and well-structured onboarding Balance your work and life with a hybrid worktime model Living and Working in Dubai Dubai is a vibrant, cosmopolitan city known for its modern architecture, luxurious lifestyle, and rich cultural heritage. Living and working in Dubai offers an exceptional quality of life with world-class amenities, a safe environment, and a thriving expatriate community. Experience a dynamic blend of work and leisure in one of the world’s most exciting cities. Ready to make a difference? Join Eaton’s Dubai Team and be part of a company shaping the future of sustainable manufacturing and power management! We are committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for job applicants and employees. Our recruitment processes use balanced selection criteria and avoid unlawful discrimination against applicants on the basis of their age, colour, disability, marital status, national origin, gender, gender identity, genetic information, race or racial origin, religion, sexual orientation or any other status protected or required by law.

jobs.title: Associate Director – Mission Critical & Data Centres (Electrical)
jobs.description: Job Description WSP in the Middle East is seeking an experienced Associate Director – Mission Critical & Data Centres (Electrical), based in Dubai, UAE, supporting the continued growth of our Building Services Data Centre discipline. You will be responsible for the end-to-end design, delivery, and technical leadership of mission-critical data centre facilities. You will act as the single technical authority, interfacing directly with clients, vendors, and internal teams to ensure projects meet performance, reliability, and compliance targets from design inception through to delivery. Responsibilities Serve as the single point of contact for all technical aspects of assigned data center projects, leading client discussions and negotiating technical scopes. Lead and approve concept, schematic, and detailed designs across electrical and mechanical disciplines, including UPS, generators, switchgear, HVAC, cooling, public health systems, Building Management Systems, fire protection and fire/life safety. Develop and standardize scalable, repeatable data center solutions to drive consistency and efficiencies across UAE and KSA. Conduct site assessments, capacity planning, and feasibility studies aligned with Uptime Institute Tier requirements. Ensure compliance with international standards (Uptime Institute, TIA-942, NFPA, ASHRAE) and local regulations. Mentor and coach engineering teams, drive knowledge transfer, and capture lessons learned for continuous improvement. Collaborate with the supervision team and other stakeholders to control costs, manage vendors, and mitigate technical risks. Drive business growth by contributing to technical proposals, client presentations, and by identifying opportunities for service enhancements Champion Engineering Standards Lead cross-regional collaboration to ensure consistency, innovation, and technical excellence in design methodologies and delivery practices across all data center projects. Cultivate Strategic Technical Partnerships Serve as a senior liaison among internal engineering teams, regional centers of excellence, external consultants, construction leads, and key stakeholders to align technical vision and drive successful execution. Oversee End-to-End Engineering Lifecycle Direct all phases of engineering and design, including site feasibility analysis, conceptual development, basis of design formulation, scope definition, and construction documentation—ensuring alignment with business objectives and performance targets. Provide Visionary Project Leadership Act as the technical authority across engineering initiatives, accountable for team outcomes related to design integrity, budget adherence, schedule management, and stakeholder coordination. Stay Ahead of Industry Evolution Maintain active engagement with the global data center engineering community to identify emerging technologies, evolving standards, and best practices that can be leveraged for continuous improvement. Demonstrate Mastery in CSA & MEP Disciplines Bring expert-level knowledge in civil, structural, architectural (CSA) and mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP) systems, with a proven track record of delivering complex, mission-critical infrastructure. Apply Advanced Engineering Analysis Tools Utilize sophisticated modeling and simulation platforms such as ETAP, 6Sigma CFD, AmpCalc, and other analytical tools to validate design decisions and optimize system performance. Qualifications Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical, Mechanical, or Building Services Engineering. 15+ years of progressive experience in planning, designing, and delivering large-scale data centers, including multiple Uptime Tier III/IV projects. Demonstrated ability to lead multidisciplinary teams and coordinate stakeholders in complex, matrixed environments. Professional certifications such as Uptime Tier Certified Professional, PMP, LEED AP, or BICSI RCDD are highly desirable. In-depth knowledge of MV/LV power distribution, UPS, emergency generators, CRAC units, economizers, chilled-water systems, VFDs, fire detection/suppression, BMS, and DCIM platforms. Strong understanding of latest Data Centre system trends and technologies such as liquid-cooling are highly desirable Preferred experience with fast track design/build projects and or multiple significant upgrade project for large-scale technical operations or large-scale compute farms Familiarity with local and international codes and standards, including NEC, IEC, ISO 50001, ISO 27001, PDPL, and ESMA. Imagine a better future for you and a better future for us all. Work on landmark projects around the world and embrace opportunities to make an even bigger impact in the communities you care about. What if you could do the best work of your life and create a legacy for yourself? With us, you can. Apply today.

jobs.title: Job Title: PMC Project Manager
jobs.location: Abu Dhabi, Abu Dhabi Emirate, United Arab Emirates
jobs.description: Title Job Title: PMC Project Manager Belong, Connect, Grow, with KBR! The KBR team delivers future-forward science, technology and engineering solutions and mission-critical services that help governments and companies around the world accomplish their most important objectives, while also helping achieve their sustainability goals. KBR Sustainable Technology Solutions provides holistic and value-added solutions across the entire asset life cycle. These include world-class licensed process technologies, differentiated advisory services, deep technical domain expertise, energy transition solutions, high-end design and engineering capabilities, and smart solutions to optimize planned and operating assets. Job Title: PMC Project Manager KBR is growing its Project Management Consultancy (PMC) team for an exciting, high profile offshore development in Abu Dhabi. The ADNOC PMC project role would be based in contractors office in Mussafah, Abu Dhabi. Job Purpose The PMC Project Manager will be responsible for the overall management, supervision and successful delivery of a major ADNOC Offshore project , ensuring that the EPC/EPCI contractor executes the project in accordance with ADNOC requirements, approved project objectives, contractual obligations, HSE standards, quality requirements, schedule and budget. The role will provide leadership to the multidisciplinary PMC team and act as a key interface between ADNOC Offshore, EPC/EPCI contractors, subcontractors, vendors and other project stakeholders . Current ADNOC Offshore PMC requirements specifically emphasize leadership of multidisciplinary teams and management across engineering, procurement, fabrication, construction, offshore installation, commissioning and handover. Key Responsibilities Project Management & Leadership Provide overall leadership and direction to the PMC project management and multidisciplinary teams. Act as the primary PMC interface with ADNOC Offshore, EPC/EPCI contractors, subcontractors and key stakeholders. Ensure successful delivery of project objectives in accordance with ADNOC requirements and the approved project execution strategy. Establish project priorities, governance, responsibilities and performance expectations. Lead project progress reviews and management meetings with ADNOC Offshore and contractors. Ensure effective coordination and integration between all engineering disciplines and project functions. Project Execution Oversee all phases of project execution, including engineering, procurement, fabrication, construction, offshore installation, hook-up, pre-commissioning, commissioning, start-up and handover. Review and monitor EPC/EPCI contractor performance against approved schedules and project objectives. Ensure engineering deliverables, procurement activities and construction activities are properly coordinated. Monitor critical project milestones and ensure appropriate corrective or recovery measures are implemented when required. Ensure effective management of interfaces between contractors, vendors, engineering teams, fabrication yards, offshore teams and operations. Oversee project completion and handover activities. Client & Stakeholder Management Maintain effective working relationships with ADNOC Offshore and all project stakeholders. Provide management with regular updates covering progress, schedule, cost, risks, opportunities and key project issues. Lead the resolution of major technical, contractual, commercial and execution issues. Ensure critical matters requiring management or client intervention are escalated appropriately. Coordinate with contractor management teams to ensure timely decision-making and resolution of project constraints. HSE & Quality Demonstrate strong and visible leadership in Health, Safety, Security and Environmental performance. Ensure HSE requirements are incorporated throughout all phases of project execution. Promote a strong safety culture within PMC and contractor organizations. Ensure contractor compliance with project quality requirements, inspection and testing plans and applicable ADNOC requirements. Monitor quality performance and ensure timely resolution of significant quality issues and NCRs. Current PMC requirements specifically highlight HSE leadership and compliance with project quality and inspection/testing requirements. Project Controls, Cost & Schedule Maintain overall oversight of project schedule, progress and cost performance. Review and challenge EPC contractor schedules, forecasts, progress measurement and recovery plans. Monitor critical path activities and major milestones. Review project cost forecasts and performance reports. Identify and manage project risks, opportunities, changes and potential claims. Ensure effective management, cost control, forecasting and commercial governance. Contracts & Contractor Management Monitor EPC/EPCI contractor performance and ensure compliance with contractual obligations. Review contractor progress, deliverables and performance against agreed KPIs and milestones. Support the assessment of variations, orders, claims and contractual matters. Ensure timely identification and mitigation of contractual and commercial risks. Coordinate with Contracts and Commercial teams on major contractual issues. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in engineering from a recognized university. Postgraduate qualification in Engineering/Project Management would be an advantage. PMP or equivalent Project Management certification is preferred. Experience Requirements Extensive experience in the Oil & Gas industry, with substantial experience in major offshore projects. Proven experience in a senior Project Manager / PMC Project Manager / Project Director-level environment. Strong experience in PMC/Client-side project management and EPC/EPCI contractor supervision. Previous ADNOC / ADNOC Offshore project experience is highly preferred. Strong offshore project experience covering engineering, procurement, fabrication, construction, installation, hook-up and commissioning. Experience with offshore facilities such as platforms/wellhead towers, offshore pipelines, process facilities and brownfield/greenfield modifications is highly desirable. Proven experience managing large multidisciplinary engineering and project teams. Strong understanding of project controls, scheduling, cost management, risk management and change management. Strong contractual and commercial awareness with experience managing EPC/EPCI contractors and subcontractors. In-depth understanding of applicable international Oil & Gas engineering standards, codes and industry practices. Excellent client-facing, leadership, communication, negotiation and decision-making skills. Key Competencies PMC / Client-Side Project Management ADNOC Offshore Project Experience EPC/EPCI Contractor Management Offshore Project Execution Engineering Management Procurement & Vendor Management Fabrication & Construction Management Offshore Installation & Hook-up Commissioning & Start-up Project Controls & Planning Cost & Schedule Management Contract & Change Management Risk Management HSE & Quality Leadership Client & Stakeholder Management Multidisciplinary Team Leadership R2130506

jobs.title: Senior Energy Consultant
jobs.location: Abu Dhabi, Abu Dhabi Emirate, United Arab Emirates
jobs.description: Job Description With over 14,000 professionals globally, GHD is a leading multidisciplinary professional services company delivering engineering, design, and advisory solutions across water, energy, resources, environment, property & buildings, and transportation sectors. Energy Overview Energy systems across the Middle East are evolving rapidly. Strong demand growth, major infrastructure investment, increasing renewable energy deployment and the growing need for storage, flexibility and digital solutions are creating new and complex requirements for how energy is planned, delivered and managed. In response to this transforming landscape, GHD is bringing together regional insight and global technical expertise to help utilities, governments, developers and major energy users address these challenges. Our work spans electricity networks, renewable energy, utility-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS), energy strategy and advisory, technical due diligence, regulatory support, grid integration, demand-side flexibility, and the energy needs of critical sectors such as data centres and water infrastructure, supporting clients throughout the lifecycle of their energy assets and systems. To strengthen GHD’s response and support the continued growth of our Middle East Energy team, we are looking for highly motivated professionals who bring sound technical judgement to help us deliver reliable, resilient, and lower-carbon solutions that create lasting benefits for our communities. Position Overview As a Senior Energy Consultant, you will lead and contribute to GHD’s energy sector work across the Middle East, applying your experience across electricity networks, renewable energy, energy storage, system integration, energy strategy and technical advisory. You will independently deliver and coordinate technical work, integrate multidisciplinary inputs and translate complex engineering matters into clear findings and practical recommendations. Assignments may span feasibility and options studies, network and substation design and delivery, technical and techno-economic assessments, due diligence, Owner’s Engineer services, procurement support and construction-stage services. The role combines technical delivery with project coordination, client engagement, proposal development and the mentoring of junior professionals. Key Responsibilities Contribute to multidisciplinary energy projects across electricity networks, Contribute to the business plan for Energy growth strategy in the Middle East with local leadership. Lead and contribute to business development activities and leading proposals to provide technical support to win and deliver projects. Lead and contribute to multidisciplinary technical workstreams across electricity networks, renewable energy, energy storage, system integration, energy strategy and related infrastructure. Deliver feasibility and options studies, engineering assessments and technical advisory assignments from initial scoping through to final recommendations. Assess project requirements, technical configurations, technology options, operational constraints and interfaces with existing infrastructure. Undertake, review or coordinate relevant technical analyses, including power-system, grid-integration, energy-modelling and techno-economic studies. Support the planning, design and delivery of electricity network and substation projects, including option selection, design coordination, technical specifications, equipment interfaces, procurement and construction-stage input. Review designs, calculations, specifications, equipment data and technical documentation for alignment with project requirements, applicable standards and good industry practice. Deliver technical due diligence and Owner’s Engineer assignments by evaluating technical, delivery and operational risks and developing proportionate recommendations. Coordinate multidisciplinary inputs and engage confidently with clients, utilities, developers, contractors and other project stakeholders. Manage assigned scopes in accordance with agreed programme, budget, quality, governance and health and safety requirements, including serving in a project manager role for projects. Prepare and review clear technical deliverables and support proposals, client development and other business development activities. Mentor junior professionals through technical review, coaching and knowledge sharing. Maintain external relationships with industry peers, OEMs, Contractors, and Clients. Contribute to the consistent application and continuous improvement of technical tools, methods and delivery standards. Experience & Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Electrical, Energy or Power Engineering, or a related discipline. A relevant postgraduate qualification would be advantageous. Minimum of eight (8) years of relevant experience in consulting, utilities, project development, engineering, EPC, Owner’s Engineer or technical advisory environments. Demonstrated technical depth in one or more areas such as electricity networks and substations, renewable energy, energy storage, grid connection, system integration, energy modelling, energy strategy, due diligence or project delivery, together with the ability to coordinate interfaces across disciplines. Ability to interpret complex technical information, identify material issues and develop clear, evidence-based recommendations. Good understanding of relevant international standards and engineering practices. Experience with Middle East utilities, regulatory frameworks or project-delivery environments would be highly regarded. Experience using, reviewing or directing work undertaken with relevant engineering, modelling or data-analysis tools, such as DIgSILENT PowerFactory, ETAP, PSS®E, PSCAD, PLEXOS, Python or similar platforms, as relevant to the candidate’s technical specialism. Strong written, presentation and client-facing communication skills, with the ability to explain complex matters clearly and contribute to proposals and business development. Good interpersonal skills; e.g., relate well to colleagues, clients and business contacts, and can influence them to achieve positive results Strong record of delivering technical excellence Proven experience coordinating multidisciplinary teams, managing concurrent assignments and exercising sound technical, commercial and professional judgement. Chartered Engineer status, or progress towards an equivalent recognised professional accreditation, would be advantageous. Fluency in written and spoken English is required. Occasional regional or international travel may be required. Why Join Us? The opportunity to lead significant energy and infrastructure projects across the Middle East, working directly with utilities, governments, developers, investors and major energy users. Access to GHD’s regional and global specialists across networks, renewables, energy storage, advisory and project delivery. A platform to strengthen your technical leadership, project management and client relationship capabilities. The opportunity to shape GHD’s regional Energy capability Structured professional development, mentoring and opportunities to work towards professional accreditation. An inclusive environment that values collaboration, technical quality and continuous learning. Join a team that values knowledge-sharing, mentorship, and professional excellence. Be part of a workplace that combines collaboration, flexibility, and connection. Join us in the office three days per week to contribute, connect and excel in our vibrant environment.

jobs.description: Responsibilities: Establish, maintain and enforce the controlled approved design baselines and effectivity rules for the UAS and key certification configurations (including prototypes and test specimens). Operate change control for certification impact by maintaining change/repair impact-to-compliance linkage (what changes, what requirements affected, what evidence must be updated). Implement and maintain the LODD DOH-required system for controlling and informing personnel of current changes in engineering drawings, specifications and design management procedures. Maintain the DOH-described record keeping system for type design and compliance documentation, ensuring that configuration references and histories remain auditable. Support conformity for certification inspections and tests by ensuring configuration identification, serialisation/effectivity, and documentation packages are correct and current. Exercise authority to place holds on evidence release when configuration/effectivity is ambiguous or when baselines are not properly controlled, and drive corrective actions. Ensure configuration-related record-keeping supports GCAA CAR 21 expectations for maintaining design information/data and Permit-to-Fly/Flight-Conditions supporting documents in an authority-accessible manner. Qualifications and Experience: Engineering degree (aerospace/mechanical/electrical/systems) or equivalent aviation technical qualification. Demonstrated experience in configuration management for complex aerospace/aviation products (preferably in a certification, flight test, or regulated engineering environment). Strong working knowledge of baseline/effectivity control, configuration identification and status accounting methods and tools (e.g., Siemens Teamcenter, Siemens Polarion, Microsoft SharePoint, Gitlab). Proven ability to maintain test article configuration indices and enforce configuration discipline for test readiness and certification evidence integrity. Experience implementing change control communication practices (ensuring teams are informed of drawing/specification/procedure changes in a controlled way). Understanding of how configuration interacts with airworthiness compliance evidence, including traceability expectations between configuration baselines and compliance documents. Strong documentation and record-keeping discipline; able to produce audit-ready configuration registers, effectivity statements and controlled histories. Ability to challenge stakeholders and stop/hold releases when configuration integrity is at risk, while driving timely resolution. Strong cross-functional coordination skills with engineering, airworthiness/compliance, flight test, and external partners/suppliers. Desirable: exposure to GCAA CAR 21 or EASA Part 21 design organisation practices and record-keeping expectations (including maintaining design information/data and, where applicable, PtF/Flight-Conditions supporting documentation).

jobs.title: Product Lead
jobs.description: About Finanshels Finanshels is a fast-growing fintech building the Financial Operating System (FinOS) for SMEs across the MENA region. We automate accounting and tax operations, deliver real-time financial health insights, and build systems which help finance teams scale efficiently. Our product operates across multiple UAE regulatory frameworks, and we build it with a small, high-ownership, AI-native team. THE OPPORTUNITY Our customers experience Finanshels through accounting, taxation, bookkeeping and more — and today that experience is fragmented, manual, and stitched across disconnected systems. Talented builders are shipping AI-powered solutions against individual pieces of it, at speed, but without a unifying product view of the journey those pieces belong to. This role exists to fix that. You will own the customer experience charter on FinOS: replacing a broken, manual journey with automated, productised, and unified experiences across every stage and every service line. Along the way, you will raise the product bar for how the whole team builds — defining the problem, the user, and the measure of success before engineering begins. This is a hands-on role in a startup. You will start as the sole product owner for this charter, reporting to the Head of Product, with scope to build and lead a product team as the function grows. What You'll Own ▸ The End-to-End Customer Journey . Map, diagnose, and rebuild the customer experience across service lines — from first touch through ongoing delivery — turning manual, fragmented steps into unified, productised flows on FinOS. ▸ Automation at the Core . Identify where human effort is absorbing what the product should do, and drive the automation that removes it — measured in customer effort reduced and operational hours freed. ▸ Consolidation onto One Platform . Bring capability scattered across legacy internal systems into a single coherent experience, so customers and the teams serving them work in one place, not many. ▸ Product Standards for AI-Native Building . Raise how the team builds. Bring rigour — clear problem definition, user clarity, success metrics, and evaluation — to AI features that today ship without it. ▸ Prioritisation and Sequencing. Decide what gets built and in what order. Protect the roadmap from work that does not move the metric, and retire builds that have stopped earning their place. ▸ Product Execution. Own roadmap and releases with Engineering, Delivery, Tax and CX. Set standards for accuracy, security, auditability and approvals. Prioritize by hours saved, reliability, customer impact and cost. ▸ Measurement. Define the metrics that describe a healthy customer journey, instrument them with our data and analytics team, and hold the roadmap accountable to them. OWNERSHIP AND AUTONOMY This role carries a clearly defined charter and the authority to run it. Within that charter you are expected to decide — on scope and sequencing, operating cadence and product rituals, user experience and workflow direction, what the team declines to build, and what gets retired. Tooling and vendor decisions sit with you within an agreed budget. Decisions that shift resources beyond your charter, affect pricing or revenue, or cannot be reversed are made jointly with the Head of Product. Everything else is yours. What We're Looking For ▸ Experience . 8+ years in product management, including a period as an early or founding product hire responsible for establishing the function. ▸ Building the Discipline . A demonstrable track record of moving a team from output to outcomes — introducing product practice where it did not previously exist, and making it stick. ▸ Commercial Judgment. You connect every product decision to a business result — revenue earned, cost removed, or time returned — and can defend the trade-off. ▸ Technical Credibility. Engineers regard you as a peer. You hold your own on architecture and data trade-offs and know when technical debt is the right call. ▸ Customer Obsession. You work close to real users — business owners, accountants, tax consultants — and can translate observed friction into shipped improvement. ▸ Journey and Service Design. Proven ability to diagnose experience failure across a complex, multi-stage, partly manual journey and redesign it as a product. ▸ AI Fluency in Practice. You have shipped AI-powered products to production and can speak credibly to evaluation, guardrails, and how you measured whether it worked. ▸ Communication. You write clearly enough that your strategy documents do not need rewriting, and you influence through evidence rather than authority. ▸ Domain (Preferred). Fintech, accounting, tax, or another regulated or professional-services environment. WHY FINANSHELS ▸ Genuine Ownership . Define the customer experience charter from the ground up. ▸ AI-First Mandate. Applied AI is not a side project — it is how we build. ▸ Lean Team, High Impact . Every person and every decision matters. ▸ Fintech at the Right Moment. Finanshels is at an inflection point, and this role will define how we scale. How To Apply Send your CV, along with anything that shows how you build — a strategy document, a before-and-after journey you rebuilt, or a product you are proud of — to careers@finanshels.com.

Under Lilly's Arm's-Length Principle, partners hold Marketing Authorization, distribute and promote Lilly's portfolio, and manage day-to-day commercial and HCP-facing execution in-market, while Lilly retains IP, sets supply price, and provides strategic and brand guidance. As the Brand Lead, Neuroscience, IBU Alliance Markets, you will be Lilly's strategic anchor for the Neuroscience portfolio — including donanemab and future pipeline assets — across this Alliance footprint. You will strengthen strategic partnerships through disciplined alliance management, lead the Neuroscience portfolio agenda on behalf of Lilly, represent the brand to partners, provide strategic guidance upon request, and help ensure launch excellence for Neuroscience products across the Alliance. You will build partner marketing capability in the Neuroscience therapeutic area and regularize 1:1 governance cadences with partner Brand/Marketing counterparts. Consistent with the Arm's-Length Principle, you will support — rather than direct — partners in the field, including on when and how to use market research, and, upon request, will help partners maximize portfolio growth by sharing Lilly's global Neuroscience experience and best practices. You will also recommend changes to internal procedures across regions to help partners comply with local regulations. Brand Lead, Neuroscience – Key Responsibilities Portfolio Strategy & Launch Excellence (Neuroscience) Apply a thorough understanding of the complexity and ambiguity of external analysis (epidemiology, competitive landscape, market research) to make Neuroscience brand/molecule recommendations, and accurately define critical success factors for the therapeutic area. Ensure ongoing communication from Lilly global Neuroscience teams is appropriately and promptly shared with partners so they remain current on global brand developments. Upon request, share product information with partners' medical, marketing and their trainers, and share Lilly's experience and learnings from prior Neuroscience product launches. Closely work with Regulatory and Medical teams to support and fast-track Neuroscience launches and life-cycle activities in Alliance countries. Partner Relationship & Capability Management Act as the subject-matter expert for the Neuroscience brand/portfolio and as the principal liaison between partner and Lilly on brand/therapeutic-area topics. Build partner marketing capability in Neuroscience — coaching partner brand teams, upon request, on brand planning, forecasting and share experience of Next-Generation Engagement Tools and materials (e.g., VAE, eP2Ps, SOAs) — while field execution and HCP engagement remain the partner's accountability under the Arm's-Length Principle. Support partners in sharing initiatives that maximize the value of Neuroscience molecules with key reimbursement/formulary and HCP stakeholders, without assuming HCP-facing responsibilities that belong to the partner. Regularize 1:1 governance cadences with partner Brand/Marketing counterparts to maintain alignment on strategy, launch readiness and performance. Measurement and Evaluation Deliver on revenue, APT (achievement to plan) and market share of the Neuroscience portfolio across Alliance partnership markets. Use measurement results defined in the partnership agreement, local customer insights and cross-market experience to effectively track progress toward agreed Neuroscience objectives. Monitor Neuroscience competitive intelligence and clinical/guideline developments and disseminate implications to partners and internal stakeholders. Compliance Operate strictly within Lilly's Alliance Arm's-Length Principle: partners hold Marketing Authorization and execute in-market promotion; Lilly retains IP, sets supply price, and provides strategic guidance rather than directing local execution. Act in accordance with privacy and other internal and external procedures, the Alliance Playbook 3.0, and the highest ethical standards of Lilly and the communities where Lilly and its partners do business. Demonstrate Lilly values with a strong commitment to ethics & compliance, minimizing risk and ensuring no violations when working with partners, including in partners' use of Next-Generation Engagement Tools. Capabilities/Skills Commercial acumen and strategic mindset, with the ability to think analytically and develop innovative solutions to complex challenges; Neuroscience disease-area or Neuroscience marketing experience is an advantage. Brand planning and forecasting (strategic planning of Neuroscience portfolio). Ability to operate effectively in a multi-cultural, multi-market environment spanning 65+ Alliance markets across various regions (ASEAN, Africa + part of Middle east and Latam), with strong interpersonal, collaboration and partnering skills and the ability to relate to and influence people at all levels. Proficient with written and spoken English; Arabic or other regional languages is a plus for MENA/Gulf-facing markets. Effective, efficient and decisive; speaks up with ideas and concerns and to help ensure the safety of others. Sound knowledge of compliance and ethical standards within the pharmaceutical industry, including Alliance Arm's-Length operating principles. Strong project management and organizational skills; good planning and decision-making. Upholds Lilly values (Integrity, Excellence, Respect); outstanding learning agility and proactiveness. Skilled at influencing with authority while working with partner brand managers and Lilly cross-functional teams (CFT). Qualifications & Experience Required Bachelor's Degree required; Pharmacy, PharmD or related field, plus MBA (Marketing) or Master's, preferred. At least 1 year of sales experience. 5+ years' experience in pharma marketing, including regional/affiliate launch experience, preferred. Responsibilities Strategy and school support Develop and deliver a coherent community outreach and National Identity strategy aligned with Aldar Education priorities and current ADEK requirements. Set clear minimum standards, annual priorities, templates and implementation guidance while allowing schools to respond to their individual context and community. Monitor each school’s National Identity strategy and annual action plan, confirming Principal approval, alignment with school improvement priorities and termly review; follow up on agreed actions. Create a network of school community and National Identity leads to share effective practice, collaborate on initiatives and provide peer support. National Identity and ADEK readiness Support schools to embed the National Identity Mark domains of Culture, Values and Citizenship, including UAE history, heritage, Arabic language, respect, compassion, global understanding, belonging, volunteering and conservation. Coordinate readiness reviews, evidence audits and school visits against ADEK expectations; track actions arising from internal review and external evaluation through to completion. Maintain current knowledge of relevant ADEK policies and evaluation expectations, communicating changes and supporting consistent implementation across schools. Maintain a central register of applicable National Identity requirements, each school’s implementation progress, supporting evidence and improvement actions; escalate unresolved gaps to the Director of Arabic & MoE Curriculum and Quality and Compliance team. Community and parent engagement Help schools map their communities and develop engagement plans that build trust, respond to local needs and widen participation among families and community stakeholders. Strengthen the role of parents as partners in learning and members of the school community, with particular attention to Emirati parent voice and involvement. Develop partnerships with relevant government, cultural, heritage, Arabic-language, higher education, charitable, volunteering, sustainability and industry organisations. Lead or coordinate group-wide campaigns, events and community programmes with clear educational outcomes, defined responsibilities and post-activity evaluation. Promote student-led volunteering, conservation and civic initiatives that develop belonging, responsibility and active citizenship. Track student participation in volunteering, cultural visits and community initiatives across schools, including equitable access and evidence of student outcomes. Quality assurance and impact Define and maintain a concise dashboard covering engagement, committee effectiveness, partnership quality, participation, school improvement actions and National Identity outcomes. Use surveys, focus groups, participation data, observations, student work and case studies to evaluate impact and inform continuous improvement. Provide termly reports to the Director of Arabic & MoE Curriculum and relevant senior stakeholders on implementation, quality, student outcomes, equitable participation, risks and improvement actions. Ensure all visits, events, volunteers and partnership activities comply with safeguarding, risk assessment, consent, approvals, records and reputational requirements. Identify professional development needs and design or commission training that enables school teams to deliver consistently high-quality provision. jobs.title: National Consultant : Domestic and Sustainable Financing for TPSR, SRHR & DD
jobs.description: Job Description Purpose of consultancy: The purpose of this consultancy is to provide expert technical leadership to drive the implementation of the Sustainable Financing Roadmap for Uganda (2026–2030), specifically linked to the Demographic Dividend domestic financing requirements. The consultant will lead evidence generation, strategic policy dialogue aligned with Uganda’s budget calendar, public financial management (PFM) assessments, and institutional capacity development to enable the Government of Uganda to: Spend More: Increase domestic budget allocations and leverage predictable resources for Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR), adolescent health, and TPSR implementation through targeted advocacy in Uganda's budget cycle. Spend Better: Diagnose Public Financial Management (PFM) bottlenecks, improve expenditure execution, equity, and efficiency across national and district local government levels. Diversify Financing Sources: Explore innovative financing, results-based mechanisms, private sector engagement, and alignment with International Financial Institutions (IFIs). Institutionalize Systems: Embed financing tools, analytics, and tracking mechanisms directly into government PFM processes to support the transition from aid funding to sustainable domestic financing. Scope of work: Background Sustainable financing is not achieved by isolated fundraising activities. It emerges when robust evidence, effective policy dialogue, stronger public financial management and diversified partnerships reinforce each other to influence government financing decisions. This consultancy will support UNFPA to strengthen Uganda's sustainable financing ecosystem for population and sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR). The consultant will support the generation and use of strategic evidence, strengthen institutional capacity, and foster policy dialogue to translate evidence on financing into sustainable public investment and long-term financing reforms. Overall Objective To lead the execution of the UNFPA CPD10 Sustainable Financing Roadmap, integrating financing analytics and driving evidence-informed policy dialogue aligned with the Public Finance Management Act (PFMA) 2015 budget calendar, and Programme-Based Budgeting (PBB) architecture, specifically under the Human Capital Development Programme Working Groups. Specific Objectives & Strategic Pillars Pillar 1: Build the Evidence & Analytics Cost of Inaction & Investment Cases: building on the existing evidence, update, adapt, and generate economic evidence/policy briefs on the cost of inaction regarding teenage pregnancy, SRHR and DD. Budget Notes & Factsheets: Develop targeted budget notes, financing factsheets, and policy briefs to quantify financing gaps and demonstrate Return on Investment (ROI) to key fiscal decision-makers. Fiscal Space & Efficiency Analysis: Identify potential fiscal space opportunities like earmarked health revenues and taxes, and model efficiency gains in current health/social sector spending. Pillar 2: Influence Public Financing – "Spend More" Primary Goal: Drive evidence-informed advocacy across critical decision points in the Ugandan budget calendar to protect, create, and scale domestic budget allocations for DD, SRHR, teenage pregnancy prevention, and TPSR implementation at national and District Local Government (DLG) levels. Q1 Touchpoint (Sept – Dec) | Budget Strategy & Budget Framework Papers (BFPs): 1st Budget Call Circular (BCC1) Engagement (Sept–Oct): Work with the Ministry of Health (Adolescent & School Health Division) and the Human Capital Development (HCD) Programme Working Group (PWG) to ensure adolescent SRHR and TPSR priorities are integrated into the Programme Budget Framework Paper (PBFP) ceilings. District Local Government (DLG) BFP Technical Support (Oct–Nov): Support key pilot/scale-up districts during regional LG budget consultations to ensure UNFPA CPD10 indicative planning figures, TPSR surveillance, and SRHR/DD indicators are captured in DLG BFPs. Cabinet & MoFPED Submissions (Dec 31): Prepare concise Budget Advocacy Briefs for MoFPED ahead of the final National Budget Framework Paper (NBFP) submission to Parliament. UNFPA CPD10 cofinancing MOUs with NPA and DLG (Dec 31): provide technical support to draft and negotiate the co-financing MOUs with MoFPED and MoLG, for the implementation of the UNFPA Country Programme 10. Q2 Touchpoint (Jan – Feb) | Parliamentary Scrutiny of the NBFP: Parliamentary "Budget Champions" Engagement (Jan): Facilitate targeted advocacy roundtables with the Parliamentary Committee on Health, Committee on Gender, Committee on Budget, and the Uganda Women Parliamentary Association (UWOPA) using Cost of Inaction and Investment Case findings. NBFP Recommendations Push (Feb 15): Provide technical inputs and draft memo language to MPs to ensure Parliamentary recommendations on the NBFP mandate higher funding allocations for adolescent health supplies (family planning/contraceptives), SGBV response, and school-based health tracking. Q3 Touchpoint (March – May) | Ministerial Policy Statements (MPS) & Appropriation: 2nd Budget Call Circular (BCC2) & MPS Finalization (March 15): Assist MoH and relevant MDAs in populating the Program Budgeting System (PBS) to ensure specific DD/SRHR/TPSR activity codes and budget lines are retained in the Ministerial Policy Statements. Sectoral Committee Hearings (April 1 – April 20): Equip civil society coalitions, youth champions, and MoH technical teams with analytical briefing kits to defend DD/SRHR lines during MPS sectoral committee reviews. Appropriation Bill Enactment (May 31): Track and verify that final parliamentary appropriations retain approved DD, SRHR and TPSR allocations prior to presidential assent. Pillar 3: Improve Spending Efficiency – "Spend Better" Primary Goal: Diagnose Public Financial Management (PFM) bottlenecks, optimize budget execution rates, and ensure public investments in DD, SRHR and TPSR yield high value-for-money and equitable outcomes across national and local government levels. Budget Execution & Release Tracking (Q1–Q4 Quarterly Cycles): Quarterly Fund Release Audits: Analyze MoFPED quarterly warranting and release performance for health and social development votes to identify delays in operational fund disbursement to central divisions and DLGs. Absorption & Execution Rate Reviews: Assess execution bottlenecks (procurement delays, late IFMS releases, cash flow constraints) affecting adolescent SRHR commodity procurement (NMS/JMS) and district TPSR operations. PFM System Diagnostics & Efficiency Analyses: Public Expenditure & Bottleneck Analysis (PEBA): Conduct a targeted PFM review of how domestic resources flow from MoFPED to MoH, MoES, MoGLSD, MoLG and downstream to District Health Teams (DHTs), health facilities, schools and other committees. Value-for-Money (VfM) & Equity Mapping: Evaluate unit costs and equity distribution of health/social sector spending to ensure funds reach high-burden, vulnerable adolescent populations (applying Leave No One Behind criteria). Efficiency Reallocation Recommendations: Identify operational double-counting or programmatic inefficiencies, providing actionable options to reallocate savings directly into core SRHR/DD/TPSR surveillance and response activities. Pillar 4: Diversify Financing Sources Primary Goal: Broaden the SRHR and adolescent health financing architecture beyond traditional public budgets by leveraging International Financial Institutions (IFIs), results-based mechanisms, and innovative private sector partnerships. IFI Portfolio Alignment (World Bank, AfDB, Global Fund, GFF): Human Capital Development Project Integration: Map ongoing and pipeline IFI loan/grant operations in Uganda (e.g., World Bank health/education projects, UgIFT, UACE) and develop technical briefs to embed TPSR and adolescent health disbursement-linked indicators (DLIs) or results conditions into IFI programs. Results-Based Financing (RBF) & Blended Finance: RBF Framework Design: Formulate concrete options for incorporating adolescent SRHR, teenage pregnancy prevention, and retention indicators into existing National/DLG Results-Based Financing frameworks. Blended & Catalytic Finance Models: Explore feasibility for co-financing mechanisms where UNFPA catalytic funds or development partner grants leverage concessional government borrowing or private sector co-investments. Private Sector & Innovative Financing Mobilization: Private Sector & CSR Mapping: Identify major private sector entities (telecoms, banking, commercial agriculture, energy) operating in Uganda with corporate social responsibility (CSR) or ESG alignment to adolescent empowerment, digital health, and SRHR. Private-Public Partnership (PPP) Models: Design investment packages for private sector participation in digital TPSR reporting platforms, adolescent-friendly health service delivery, or skill-building initiatives for young mothers and youth. Clarify consultant’s scope of work and identify touchpoints requiring UNFPA staff input. Endline Training (Phase 6): Technical transfer of developed econometric models and analytical tools to ensure long-term government and staff ownership. It will also evaluate the impact of the consultancy’s deliverables on recent policy outcomes and establish strategies for sustaining evidence-informed advocacy in future budget cycles. Geographic Coverage The consultancy will focus at national level and specifically on the 13 SAY Plus + programme districts in West Nile, Acholi, Karamoja, Bukedi and Busoga. Evaluation Approach and Methodology The consultant will employ a mixed-methods, health economics, and public financial management approach, including the following: Quantitative Fiscal & Budget Analysis: Expenditure tracking, budget execution modeling, fiscal space assessments, and investment case recalculations. Political Economy & Stakeholder Analysis: Mapping budget decision-makers, incentive structures, and distributive bargaining dynamics within health and fiscal planning cycles. Systems Analysis & PFM Audits: Evaluating resource flows, release schedules, and administrative bottlenecks from central ministries down to District Local Governments (DLGs).
